stages.ignored: A Merovingian claimant appears, and the Church, the nobility and the Quaesitores turn on the Order.
stages.stopped: The claimants are thwarted quietly, without a charge of scrying.
stages.turned: The covenant shapes the boy's future, and with it perhaps a kingdom's.

stages.title: Reims
stages.clues: The plots come due together at the cathedral where the kings are anointed.
stages.ignored: The succession breaks, or a false king is anointed.
stages.stopped: The oil and the throne are kept safe, and the Order's hand stays hidden.
stages.turned: The characters learn the secret of kingship, and must decide what to do with it.

neighbours.secrets: Behind the king's bad counsel is a truly evil man on his staff, prompted by a demon.

neighbours.name: The Advance of the Dominion
neighbours.summary:
A saga frame, as the central arc or as a background theme. Towns grow, and each one turns the land for twenty miles round into farmland under the Dominion, which hampers magic and wears away vis sites. Paris, as big as some kingdoms, is a diamond the magi long for and cannot grasp, and anything that harms it harms the many covenants that buy rare supplies there. The royal court has settled in Paris, drawing the great lords there and leaving their lands to stewards who are easier to suborn but punish harder. The French Church grows rich and spends on good works that spread the Dominion, though its quarrel with the pope gives magi room to settle scores.

Covenants work through masks, mundane agents who can be dropped or killed: Confluensis among the Seine shippers and the law faculty, Fudarus in the Dyers' Guild and the fashionable clothiers, Eboris among the ivory carvers and the underworld, Montverte in the Hanse Parisienne, Oleron with sailors' gangs. Eboris is senex of Paris, so proxy wars there are now illegal, and Eboris may raise the alarm if something monstrous threatens the city.

details.antagonist: The spread of towns, fields and the Dominion

stages.title: The plough's twenty miles
stages.clues: New fields creep towards a covenant vis site and its aura weakens. On a winter night of storm the liege lord brings a covenant knight a swaddled child to hide and raise as his own, and will not say why.
stages.ignored: A vis source fails, and the child's secret finds the covenant.
stages.stopped: The covenant protects its sites, by law, purchase or cunning.
stages.turned: The covenant moves its harvests, or learns who the child is.

stages.title: War!
stages.clues: After years of peace, neighbouring lords raid, vassals rebel, crops burn and castles are besieged, but only the covenant's mundane holdings are hit, as Normandy's Code allows. A Hermetic rival is suspected.
stages.ignored: The covenant's mundane base is destroyed and the covenant falls.
stages.stopped: The rival is found and turned away.
stages.turned: The covenant turns the rival's mundane allies against him.

stages.title: Threats to Paris
stages.clues: Something menaces Paris: a preacher bent on reducing the city to joyless prayer, a ring of diabolists in its court, guard or clergy, plague, famine, invasion by a rebel duke or a foreign king, or riots of merchants against nobles or French against foreigners. Eboris calls for help.
stages.ignored: Paris suffers, and with it every covenant that depends on it.
stages.stopped: The city is saved, though the Dominion hampers every spell.
stages.turned: The covenant gains masks and influence in Paris.

stages.title: Moral hazard
stages.clues: Nobles who know the Order offer covenants under pressure what they need in return for help, as Henry II and Philip did in their war, when Oleron was censured for trying to free Eleanor of Aquitaine. Liege covenants raise their prices.
stages.ignored: Weakened covenants slip into alliance with the crown or a rebel; the Quaesitores' fears come true.
stages.stopped: The covenant refuses, and finds its own way to endure.
stages.turned: The covenant becomes a liege that profits from others' weakness, or joins a colonial venture abroad.

stages.title: The cracking of old wards
stages.clues: As magic fails, ancient wards fade. In a sea cave at the end of a promontory in the Vendée a demon, maddened by the sea, bellows at high tide and hurls spray over the cliffs; it is held by a Magical ward, which the coming Dominion will wear away faster than it harms the demon.
stages.ignored: The ward breaks and the demon goes free.
stages.stopped: The ward is renewed or the demon destroyed.
stages.turned: The weakened site, empty of its old prisoner, becomes a home for a new covenant.

neighbours.secrets: The strong will prey on the weak: young covenants become vassals at a rising price, some lieges fail, and some covenants may seek lieges outside the Tribunal. A coalition may set out to colonise Denmark, West Africa or a vis-rich Tribunal. Old wards set in the Schism War or the Corruption of Tytalus will crack as the Dominion rises.

characters.name: Buliste

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Prima of House Tytalus, Buliste filia Bulcis, who led the House for twenty years before a long Twilight left her seeming dead. She wore the Circlet of the Primus as it began, Harpax could not take it from her, and she wears it still, setting the covenant's invisible spirits to plague her rival: they pull stones from his unfinished tower, put ground glass in his food, sew up his clothes, and play countless other tricks that border on the deadly. More important to the House, she runs Fudarus's vast web of spies and speaks mind to mind with several of its key agents, through her mastery of Mentem and a collection of fixed Arcane Connections; that keeps her respected across the Order, though she has little power in the Normandy Tribunal. Her followers, the Fideli, rally to her purple banner. Her challenges to visitors are philosophical or magical.

She looks a regal woman in her sixties, stout but not fat, in violet satin and white Breton lace, with a very expressive face. Her plainest Twilight scar is that her kindness and her anger can both be felt, the one gently, the other painfully. Older than Harpax, she has the more raw power, but several Twilights have hemmed in her magic.
characters.secrets: She is steering Harpax toward a Diedne relic so she can frame him with it.

characters.name: Harpax

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Primus of House Tytalus, the tenth, Harpax filius Bulcis, who always felt held back by his elder 'sister', fought her hard for the House and lost. When she seemed to die he barely paused before breaking into her sanctum and taking the Rod of the Primus, and took over her role as Lord Heusaff. He torments her with the Rod: one day her sanctum is hot enough to melt her candles, the next she must break ice on her washbasin.

He reads Tribunal politics and his fellow Tytali's plots better than Buliste, governs the covenant's wealth in vis and coin, keeps the oaths of its two vassals, and has bought many magi's loyalty; his Decimi, who wear the tenth Primus's sigil, are the stronger party in Normandy. Without the spies he cannot steer much of the House's business. More careful and more varied than his sister, he has a wider stock of spells and enchantments but less depth in the Arts. His challenges to visitors are physical.

As himself he is a distinguished, stick-thin man who looks about fifty and suffers some arthritis; he keeps other guises too, and may first be met as a butler, a sentry or a tinker. His obsession and sigil is plurality, and his Twilight scar makes the cut of his clothes drift through the day, always in his forest green.
characters.secrets: As Lord Heusaff he takes the shape of a dashing young nobleman, and has played the part so well that he has had to cultivate unpleasant habits to keep off marriageable women.

characters.name: Adanos Lutorum

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Tytalus, the youngest of Exspectatio's founders, with the blood of an earth spirit and a deep affinity for soil, stone and clay: over seven feet tall, entirely hairless, with skin like rock. He has backed Harpax staunchly ever since Buliste refused to take him as her apprentice. In any contest, of blows, words or magic, he lets his opponent wear herself out against his unbreakable defences and then strikes one crushing blow. He is Iasper's master, and wrote The Mole's Work, Terram Lab Texts now held for the Tribunal. Looks about forty.
characters.secrets: Like Valerian of Confluensis, he is reputed to belong to the Guernicus Terrae cult.

characters.name: Kybella

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Of House Tytalus, a leading member of the Titanoi, the House's cult of theurgists, and a close friend of Prima Buliste. She keeps up the enchantments that hold Fudarus's spirits in check and casts its Aegis of the Hearth each year for both Primi. She specialises in genii loci and searches every place she stays for signs of one. Her filius Helios, of Atramentum Renatus, is a theurgist too. Looks about fifty.
characters.secrets: Twelve years ago a Twilight showed her Death reaping Europe, kings, bishops, commoners and magi alike, and she founded the Cabal of the Laden Cart to trap Death and hold it to ransom. The other members assume she is one of them but never know which disguise is hers. With another theurgist of her line she is obsessed with the Ankeu, and her agents listen across Brittany for anyone who hears its cart.

characters.name: Iasper filius Adanos

description.biography: Self-Confident is his House Virtue. The book prints Concentration 2+2 and Terram 6+3, the bonuses being his Puissant Concentration and Puissant Terram. Combat: fist Init -2, Attack +1, Defense 0, Damage 0; Soak +2. Appearance: thin, unshaven, with long, unkempt black hair, yet always impeccably dressed.

characters.summary: Of House Tytalus, the youngest of Exspectatio, four years past his Gauntlet, a thin man with long shaggy black hair and stubble whose clothes are always immaculate. He is all contrasts: his magic is at once tightly harnessed and unpredictable, and he prides himself on self-control while delighting in turmoil and chaos, with a knack for Terram from his master. He holds that reined chaos is the road to knowing oneself and, unlike most Tytali, stirs up conflict beyond his power to control, taking the vagaries of chance as lessons. He means no harm but seldom thinks what his deeds do to others. He is close to his family, the Foutins, a large clan of local brawlers and ne'er-do-wells who are not quite criminals but find trouble easily, and he seeks to join the Cabal of the Laden Cart.

characters.name: Geirlaug

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Leader of Montverte for more than half a century, an archmaga of House Flambeau of the founder Harivald's line, plainly a supreme master of Ignem, and the third eldest magus of the Tribunal. Her age is uncertain (perhaps 150, apparently in her mid-sixties). Erratic and marked by long Twilights whose dates no one knows, she hardly ever leaves her tower and is said to have come to depend on fire: great flames are often seen inside it.

She attends council only as an image in a great mirror at the head of the table, an elegant, stern old woman with blazing eyes, the flames behind her moving with her mood: lucid, cryptic, silent or absent. The others privately doubt her sanity, but she tolerates no defiance and the council does her will. She hates Oleron almost beyond reason for an insult from its old leader decades ago, and dislikes the other lieges.

characters.name: Thormod

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Filius of Geirlaug and her opposite: meticulously neat, his feelings and plans always hidden (he looks 48). Thought to specialise in Perdo, though nothing is really known of his tastes. He never seems to doubt or falter, which makes him secretly the most hated and feared magus of Montverte. He is the covenant's Hermetic ambassador, coldly efficient, and directs its vassals. Alone on the council he seems quite untroubled by Geirlaug and trusts her rule completely; if anyone knows her true state, it is he, and he says nothing.
characters.secrets: He is a leading member of the Children of Odin, practises Viking magic and bends his influence to the cult's ends; he may be related to its hierophant, Queen Skuld, by blood or by a tryst.

characters.name: Eduardus

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Steward of the castle, trained in House Jerbiton and a Tytalus for some decades (he looks 43): cultured, artistic and Gently Gifted. As steward he wears the persona of Edward so constantly that no one can tell him from the real Eduardus, of whom little is known. His chief task is to manage the baron, and through him the covenant's dealings with the world; a trusted adviser of the family, he is often at the baron's side. He also keeps the castle running. Edward is sociable, smooth-tongued and a seducer, and the covenfolk women he has charmed bring him the gossip that keeps him informed.

One of the few purple Fideli, who back Buliste as the true Prima of House Tytalus, and a follower of the Hippian school.

characters.name: Rotgiers de Gerberoy

description.biography: Single Weapon is 5, +2 from Puissant Single Weapon. Combat: mace and heater shield mounted Init -2, Attack +15, Defense +13, Damage +10 (on foot Attack +12, Defense +10); lance and heater shield mounted Init -1, Attack +16, Defense +13, Damage +7; Soak +11, before his items' bonuses. Equipment: full chain mail imbued with protective effects, a heater shield, a lance, and an ornate jewelled mace enchanted as his talisman; Encumbrance 2 (4). Familiar: Simo, an ancient warhorse. Twilight Scars: weak-willed people feel an unnatural fear of him, his old wounds bleed again when his magic tires him badly, metal he wears never rusts, and he cannot hear compliments.

characters.summary:
Senior Tremere of Montverte, in charge of its martial affairs: its defences, mundane and magical, and its raids, which he runs ruthlessly but with fair treatment of his victims. A huge, gruff, grey-bearded man who looks about fifty, he lives as a knight, and the baron counts him one; abroad he rides in mail with a jewelled mace and a great shield bearing Montverte's arms, at home he wears charcoal Tremere robes over a nobleman's finery. His familiar is Simo, an ancient warhorse. He holds the sigils of most of the Tribunal's few Tremere.

A feared champion of the Tourney, above all in the joust and certamen: his lance strikes true through the usual Rego Terram defences, and he can conjure a lance of bone that ignores them. He is not above a little cheating, having servants gather an Arcane Connection to an opponent for use with a figurine, or quietly stripping a rival's protections with Wind of Mundane Silence.

characters.name: Runild

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: The youngest councillor (she looks 43), quiet and unassuming beside the other four. She oversees the covenant's magical resources: its library, its vis stores and the seasons of labwork the junior magi must give. She has just finished training her first apprentice but has no voting sigil of her own yet. Her familiar, a black cat, is descended from Jerbiton's familiar, and she keeps company with all of Montverte's many cats.

characters.name: Caprican of Merinita

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Leader and champion of Oleron, apparently about fifty-five, who fought as a mercenary in the wars of the faerie courts in his youth. The last champion, afraid of dying unbeaten (with unknown results), asked him to take the seat. His wife is the faerie queen Lysette and he has an infant daughter, Columbine, whose birth tells him he will likely lose the seat within a few decades.

He follows other magi's careers and gossip closely to guess who his heir will be, and may groom a likely candidate. He dislikes Tytalus magi and would use Wizard's War, even war between covenants, to stop his heir coming from that House, for his daughter must love whoever wins her, and he cannot see how a woman could be happy wed to a creature of strife.

He has Strong Faun Blood, and his magic bends the emotions of people and animals. He belongs to the Keepers of a Thousand Tales.
characters.secrets: While Fudarus is empty and its leaders feud, he has helped other covenants take its resources and has added and fortified vassals. He expects reprisals if Tytalus finds out, and is untroubled: with Ushant so near, attacks will come anyway.

characters.name: Amelie of Merinita

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Oleron's usual spokeswoman and traveller. She is short and slight; river-nymph blood leaves her naturally bald, which she hides with illusory blonde hair, and her fingers and toes are webbed, so she always wears mittens and shoes in public.

She is no great negotiator and knows it, so she lets deals fail or sends partners to Caprican, and uses her office mostly as an excuse to see interesting places and people. Her magic is Aquam, above all the making of unnatural liquids.

characters.name: Quintinus of Verditius

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
An odd Verditius, apparently thirty-five, drawn to Oleron by magical brewing, especially with cider; when a member skilled in such things died he asked to join and take over the dead magus's laboratory. He now builds the new Stone Couches to the Queen's design, finds it far more rewarding than making enchanted items, and may soon ask to change Houses.

He stays out of his House's games of status, which spares him his Housemates' enmity, but his silence about the Couches makes him look idle or incompetent, and his standing in the House is very poor.

characters.name: Regulus of Merinita

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The Bee King: blond, amber-eyed and golden-skinned, smelling faintly of candles, and looking no more than twenty-one. His looks come of Strong Faerie Blood: he is a Bee King, a creature so rare that some Merinita think one is made when a young woman swallows a drone from a faerie hive, the steeds of the tiny knights of a sprite queen whose court wanders Mythic Europe.

A Bee King never seems to age but dies of a swift illness a century after birth if nothing kills him first. He can command any bees to do anything they can, even to their deaths, gives long messages through a bee on his tongue, understands hives and reads the bees he touches, and is never stung. He turns the grove's Herbam vis into honey holding Animal vis, and his bees build the wax statues in the chase.
characters.secrets: Two Bee Kings can never meet: if Regulus comes within scent of the hive-girl he will fall into a murderous rage and have to kill her. She is the child of faeries like him, or his own by some forgotten affair; he wants her raised happily far away, and watched, for he has never heard of a human Bee Queen.

characters.name: Luna of Bjornaer

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A noble rat. Born in Sicily of mixed Italian and Arab stock, dark-haired and dark-eyed and just under five feet tall, she dresses in few layers so as to slip in and out of her heartbeast. She has no talisman yet and is looking for something to enchant.

She trained first in the Beast Master tradition of House Ex Miscellanea; Micropedus drew out her heartbeast and got her accepted, if not respected, in his House, whose members think a rat heartbeast freakish. She thinks rats noble: sneaky, tenacious, hardy and made for living beside wasteful humans. Micropedus grooms her as his heir. At least an hour a week, and whenever she is stressed, she sits as a rat on a rafter of the covenant's granary gazing at more food than a rat could eat in a century.

Animal is her best Art, the rest learned piecemeal for useful tricks. She has mastered a spell to tunnel through stone or wood in rat form. Her combat spells are weak, but she can still call and command animals and defends herself with hordes of rats.

characters.name: Micropedus of Bjornaer

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
The Starling, Nidi's leader, apparently sixty. He spends much of his time as a bird and finds it ever harder, slower and more painful to change back as his Warping grows; a Twilight Scar leaves patches of feathers on his scalp in human form. His name, small feet, comes from another scar: his heartbeast looks like the footless starling of folklore, and his feet have shrunk with age to a child's; he suspects they will drop off when he enters Final Twilight.

The idea that small covenants can live in the uncharted spaces of towns is his. He has written on it at length and trained a few apprentices, though many Bjornaer reject it. An Auram magus skilled at weather, he breaks droughts with rain and kills grain blight with frost; the prosperity this brought is arguably why a town grew so close to the covenant.

characters.name: Viviana of Ex Miscellanea

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Spiritual leader and guide of Atsingani, a fading beauty of Mediterranean blood who looks about forty-one: filia of Aureliana, the eldest of the founders, and a soothsayer and healer of the same Byzantine tradition. She owns the covenant's most prized possession, a grand wagon of faerie make, far larger inside than out and richly fitted, with room for a laboratory and a bedchamber; it never runs out of fresh clothes and linen for her, and rides so smoothly over rough roads that nothing inside is jolted.

characters.name: Jacques of Flambeau

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Captain of the covenant's mercenaries, apparently thirty-nine. Already a seasoned Brabançon warrior, he was apprenticed at eighteen to an Ex Miscellanea eremite, so he is only some ten years past his Gauntlet. As soon as he became a magus he left his pater's covenant to rejoin his own people, and soon after joined House Flambeau. He burns to avenge his father on the Capuchonnes who killed him in 1183.

characters.name: Baudouin

description.biography:
Age 32. His Weakness is for loose women. Bows is 5, +2 from Puissant Bows.
Dagger: Init 0, Atk +9, Def +6, Dam +4. Axe and round shield, mounted: Init +1, Atk +17, Def +14, Dam +7; on foot: Init +1, Atk +14, Def +11, Dam +7. Crossbow: Init +5, Atk +16, Def +10, Dam +8. Soak +7; Encumbrance 2 (3); Fatigue OK, 0, -1, -3, -5, Unconscious. Wounds: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).
Equipment: partial leather scale armour, axe, round shield, crossbow, and a grog's pack with carpenter's tools and his lucky dice.

characters.summary: One of Atsingani's more experienced Brabanters, in its service since his youth, when he was branded a thief. A shifty man with an unkempt beard, fierce blue eyes and a face marred by the brand, he handles his weapons like an expert. Banditry is second nature, but he is tired of the wandering, the on-and-off poverty and the lack of women. Reliably violent but no leader, he is usually picked for the vanguard of a raid.

characters.name: Mathieus of Constantinople

params.group: the Paris court and its artists

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Leader of Eboris and Warden of Paris, an archmagus, filius of Maria of Constantinople; apparent age 65. A scion of a Constantinopolitan noble house who plays the exiled lord, he follows the Jerbiton idea of sufficiency: he knows enough magic to live as he likes, and more study would only fool bigger crowds or win more certamen. Long bored by magic, he spent years in the vices of the rich; now he has goals he doubts he will reach.

He backs the French crown, whose strength is remaking Paris into a city that could foster great beauty, which sets him against agents of the great dukes, of England and of Italian princes. He backs the Antigones, the rising Jerbiton generation, hoping they will mend an Order he thinks the best but a weak tool for peace. And he loathes Venice and the covenants he blames for the Fourth Crusade, supporting the French Church as a weight against Venice's hold on the pope and distrusting the Roman covenants with chapter houses in Venice. He is a master of illusion and of casting in a city.
characters.secrets: He named Constantina his heir mostly to stop people pestering him, and could be talked into naming someone who offers him a genuinely new experience.

characters.name: Marcus of Paris

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 40 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary:
Redcap and Mathieus's chief servant, the majordomo of Eboris (the book does not say whether he has the Gift). He sells news of Paris to other covenants, haggling every contract, from a weekly letter to the recovery of private papers, and sometimes passes the work to the young magi. When the nobles go home to their own lands he hires local magi's servants to keep watch on them for his clients.

He also recruits: of the many odd characters who drift to Paris he picks the best, teaches some a little Latin and places them with covenants across the Tribunal for a fee from either side. A young covenant can get a full household from him, of very colourful pasts.

characters.name: Somnifer of Merinita

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A master of dream magic, apparent age 30. During the captivity he sent his mind out in spirit form into the dreams of those he met and so kept the covenant informed of the world. He found his apprentice Languidus through dreams, lured him to the regio and trained him through the mirror in the hut that was his schoolroom and scriptorium. Warping blurs dream and waking for him, and it is hard to tell whether he is awake or sleepwalking.

With Renita dead and Stellatus gone to Iberia, he is next after Celeres of Cunfin in the line of eldest magi from which the Praeco is named.
characters.secrets: Proctor, who wants a Praeco he can trust or control, finds Somnifer as awkward a choice as Celeres.

characters.name: Mnemon of Tytalus

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A master of Rego, apparent age 60. He was a year short of his Gauntlet when the regio closed (the book's age for him fits that badly), and has never really lived his House's culture of conflict. Searching for a way out, he grew expert in spells of transport; he made the mirror that is now the covenant's gate and negotiated the new terms with Candidus. Walking and running exasperate him, and he has an unsettling habit of popping across a room or snapping objects into his hand.
characters.secrets: Nobody knows what he promised Candidus. Once someone takes his place he must carry out a fearsome task the faerie bound him to, which could fall on a player covenant.

characters.name: Rhesus

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Leader of Florum's magi: clean-shaven and muscular, looking about fifty-four. He came from the Roman Tribunal, partly to escape the professional jealousies of his House and partly because he is a weaver himself and wanted to study the spider-kin; the magical uses of flax are his chief interest. He backs the Lotharingian cause because he is weary of Normandy's ways, which make him defend resources that any other Tribunal would simply grant him.

characters.name: Calvinus

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A middle-aged magus with the Gentle Gift, looking about forty-five. Ghent knows him as 'Uncle Calvin', younger brother of Piet de Spinnen's late father, back from decades of trade in Italy, whose money is said to have paid for the Farm's last building; Piet plainly heeds his advice. A private man who reads a great deal and is said to speak five languages, he often negotiates or interprets for his nephew. Trained in urban magic like many Jerbiton, he is skilled at illusion, at spying on the covenant's mundane rivals, and at arranging crimes. His apprentice Sophia is charming and as bookish as he is, so that her cousins fear she will never marry.
characters.secrets: Piet is really his son Petrus. His Italian wife was invented, and the 'daughter' who has just arrived in Ghent, supposedly raised by equally invented grandparents, is Sophia.

characters.name: Alroy

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Florum's champion, for Normandy's habit of fighting over resources means most covenants need one: an older Flambeau, looking about sixty, with a distinguished war record in the Levant. Five years ago he decided to take an apprentice and chose Florum because it was rich, comfortable, far from the Saracens, and offered the odd Tourney. He has outlived his own expectations and killed most of what once frightened him; he hopes raising an apprentice and fighting Tytalus magi will rekindle him, a man of eager passions trying to shake off a veteran's boredom.

characters.name: Prunellie

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
An elderly maga, looking about sixty-one, who travels the Low Countries studying their peculiar faerie realm. Here, she teaches, the old gods and ancestral trees made a pact with the coming Church: faeries helped spread the Dominion and tame the forests, teaching men to clear woods, plough, sow wheat and flax and drive piles for dikes; one brought flax, a gnome invented starch, and the kabouters, a dwarfish folk, gave a hundred bells to the missionaries they favoured, and sang the first carillon of the Low Countries under a gnome's baton. Faeries who refused were hunted down by saints whom the friendly ones guided, and lie now as lone stones in the fields.

Her House thinks her interest in urban faeries a little odd, but she is firmly allied with a tribe of kabouters and has taught others her urban faerie magic. She picked the Farm's site over an old kabouter workshop. She backs the Lotharingian Tribunal because she believes the faeries' strange surrender to the Divine belongs to Flanders, Brabant and perhaps Frisia alone.
characters.secrets: She could restore the stone faeries but usually harvests them for vis instead.

characters.name: Piet de Spinnen
characters.summary: The head of the de Spinnen family, Florum's landlords and public face in Ghent, and its willing spokesman. Rivals sneer at him as old Arne de Spinnen's bastard, which also explains his keen interest in the Church's works. He has several children, two of whom spent a year at the new university in Paris.
characters.secrets: He is Petrus, the mundane son of Calvinus of Jerbiton, born at Valnastium; a successful mercenary in Italy who made dangerous rivals, faked his death, and was trained by an old Redcap to be the heir the childless Arne needed. He is very content with how his life has turned out. His two children went on from Paris to Valnastium to train as servants of House Jerbiton.

characters.name: Eulogius

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Leader of Requies Aeterna and perhaps the last founder of the Donatores living; his age is uncertain, and he looks a hundred and four. His great days of hunting the restless dead are long past, and Final Twilight is probably near. His worst Twilight scars are a body slowly turning to a corpse, impossibly gaunt with dead, withered skin, and a pain in sunlight that keeps him in his underground sanctum. He remains an unequalled banisher, a master of Perdo, Corpus and Mentem.

characters.name: Henri

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 40 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Eulogius's youngest filius and his helper, a Donator who stays mostly from duty to his tradition, and has made himself keeper of the covenant's library and lore for the generations to come.

characters.name: Eloi

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Founder of Cunfin and the man who holds it together, looking about fifty-two. To the monks he is Brother Eligius, their prior, loved for his devotion and sought for his wise counsel; to the magi he is a magus deeply anxious about the Order's standing with the Church. He sees himself as a follower of St. Nerius, bridging the Magic and the Divine, and his charm and faith bind the covenant's quarrelsome members together.

A younger son of minor nobles meant for the priesthood, he was found by Jerome of Jerbiton and trained as a magus instead, serving Jerome usefully at Confluensis but never reconciling his Gift with his wish to serve God. Meeting Angelus in 1191 showed him a way: he joined the abbey, founded the covenant with Jerome's blessing, and was soon elected prior. He uses Holy Influence to calm the Dominion about the abbey.

Close to the Priory of St. Nerius without belonging to it, he wants Nerius recognised by the Latin Church, but above all wants peace between Order and Church, and uses his weight in the Cistercian Order to head off quarrels between magi and clergy. With Jerome and Proctor he was one of the three pillars of the late Praeco's Tribunal, its link to the Church. His present worry is the new Dominicans and their zeal against heresy.
characters.secrets: He is Jerome's chief partner in hiding rescued heirs, which is very likely a breach of the Code; it brought Artorius to Cunfin.

characters.name: Angelus

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A holy hermit of House Ex Miscellanea who looks about seventy-five and lives alone in a cave above the abbey, contemplating God. The Order's only record of him is from the Tribunal of 1144, where he appeared once and then dropped out of sight; he had not left his cave for decades when Eloi found him in 1191, told him of St. Nerius and showed him the abbey and its regio. At the next Tribunal Cunfin was recognised with the two of them as founders.

He holds that Magic flows from the Divine and that Twilight is a glimpse of the face of God: a blessing God gives, but one it is sinful to seek, since only God judges who is worthy. He takes little part in the covenant's affairs, though Eloi and even Celeres come to him for counsel. He alone of Cunfin's magi lacks the Gentle Gift.
characters.secrets: He will not speak of his lineage; Eloi believes his parens was Valoran, filius of St. Nerius himself.

characters.name: Celeres

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
A magus of House Bonisagus perhaps a hundred and fifty years old (the book is not sure) and looking a hundred: since Renita's death and Stellatus's departure for Iberia, the eldest magus of the Tribunal and so first in line to be Praeco, to the dismay of Confluensis, whose magi fear his eccentricity and his hold over Cunfin's Redcaps.

Late in the twelfth century he found a copy of Chretien's Perceval and was seized by the riddle of the Grail. He gathered every book on Arthur, the Round Table and the Grail he could, and when he heard of Cunfin, with its monks and holy hermit, it seemed a page from the romances: he came at once in 1199 and talked Eloi into admitting him. He rebuilt the regio as a castle and calls the Redcaps his knights, who bring him every rumour of the Grail.

No longer hoping to find it, he now thinks the Grail may be beyond finding, and wants instead to understand it and share what he learns. He is writing a great Grail cycle on its spiritual meaning, coloured by Cistercian thought, and hopes his last apprentice Artorius will finish it if he cannot. Many doubt his wits; no one doubts his scholarship. He has the Gentle Gift, a playful humour, and is one of the covenant's champion hastiludium team.

characters.name: Hervé filius Évrard

description.biography: Equipment: a set of enchanted devices for a trading Redcap, with the effects Scales of the Magical Weight (InVi 5), Sense the Nature of Vis (InVi 5), Posing the Silent Question (InMe 20) and Trust of the Childlike Faith (PeMe 10), each at Penetration 0 with 24 uses a day. Combat: dodging, Initiative 0, Defense +3; Soak +0. Encumbrance 0.

characters.summary:
Hervé le Brun, a Redcap of the Founder's blood and son of Évrard de Tours: a stocky man with dark brown hair and olive skin who looks like his father and dresses, as he does, in plain town clothes. His soothing manner hides a calculating, driven mind.

He has always felt his father favoured his foster brother Renaud, an un-blooded foundling Évrard knew would face obstacles in the House. At the University of Paris, where Renaud breezed through his studies on wit and wine while Hervé fought with a Latin he never mastered, and where Renaud joined the Goliards without losing his father's support, Hervé vowed to outdo him.

No scholar, he is a shrewd judge of people and a fine negotiator who always comes away from the fairs with a profit. He now runs the temporary Mercer House at the Champagne fairs, the post Renaud wanted, but his father has still not given him the recognition he craves, and he has his eye on higher places in House Mercere.

characters.name: Artorius filius Celeres

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A magus of House Bonisagus newly through his Gauntlet. Eloi brought him to Cunfin as an orphan of sixteen, meaning to train him as his own successor, but Celeres announced he needed a squire and claimed the boy as his own apprentice. At his Gauntlet, his knighting as Celeres puts it, his parens named him after the legendary king of Britain. He has the Gentle Gift; his plans are his own.
characters.secrets: He is one of the heirs Jerome saved from death for their birthright and hid with Eloi's help; whose heir he is, the book does not say.

characters.name: Évrard de Tours

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary:
Redcap of House Mercere and the Tribunal's senior Redcap, the only one at Cunfin who served at the old Mercer House in Tours. He moved the House to Cunfin, rebuilt its network and trained its Redcaps, and now wants to retire: his only duty is to watch over the Mercere Portal to Dragon's Rest. He looks under fifty, having begun a longevity ritual late in life.

He trained both Cunfin's other Redcaps, his son Hervé and the foundling Renaud, and passed his post at the fairs to Hervé. After so long in a monastery he finds Celeres's playful humour a relief and spends much time with him.

characters.name: Renaud Fouinon

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 33 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: Redcap of House Mercere, a foundling Eloi brought to the covenant, trained by Évrard and raised as Hervé's foster brother. Naturally clever, he drank and slept his way through the University of Paris and joined the Goliards, which most likely cost him the post at the Champagne fairs that went to Hervé. He now roams France enjoying himself, and is proud to be one of Cunfin's hastiludium team with Celeres and Eloi, which has won three times running.

characters.name: Helios filius Kybella

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 38 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A theurgist of House Tytalus and co-founder of both Atramentum and Atramentum Renatus. He is fascinated by the schemes of the fallen Diedne covenant of Bibracte and its cult of Vercingetorix, and is trying to learn whether its magi succeeded in raising the hero's spirit.

characters.name: Gulo Midusulfis

These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 37 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A magus of House Bjornaer and co-founder of Atramentum and Atramentum Renatus. A Quaesitor wants to know whether the reports of a wild beast ravaging the country round the covenant mean that Gulo has broken the Code.

characters.name: Iacula

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 40 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A maga of House Bonisagus who joined Atramentum Renatus after its founding. She is absorbed in the study of how thrown and shot things fly, and her research has produced several spells with great martial potential.

characters.name: Philip

characters.summary: A magus of House Ex Miscellanea and one of the Donatores, a tradition that seeks to lay the restless dead to rest. Lately of Requies Aeterna, he has only just joined Atramentum Renatus. He shares Helios's interest in Bibracte but fears his colleague's work is stirring its ghosts to anger.

characters.name: Proctor

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Presiding Quaesitor of the Normandy Tribunal for its last two meetings and, since Renita's death, acting leader of Confluensis. Against his House's custom of rotating the post, he seems unlikely to let anyone else be chosen next time; his filius Aristarcus would follow him. Tytalus diabolists killed his grandparens, and his parens passed on a hatred of that House, so he deeply mistrusts the Tribunal's Tytalus magi. A strict upholder of the Code and a firm Transitionalist, he may yet be driven to extreme measures by his suspicion. He looks about sixty: weathered face, leathery hands, pale skin, a white beard and no moustache, and a favourite slate-green robe fastened with two crossed pins shaped as swan feathers, one lead and one ivory. His familiar is a sacred ibis from his wandering youth. His talisman is a brass fool's bell that jingles in his pocket; he believes it one of the bells Richard the Devil wore doing penance in Rome, and it is enchanted against the Infernal. Those he distrusts are not told, and many think he carries it as a reminder not to act the fool.

characters.name: Aristarcus

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Filius of Proctor and the Tribunal's usual prosecutor, with unrivalled rhetoric. He does not share his parens's distrust of House Tytalus and leans Traditionalist, but the two are frequent allies in their faith in the law. A strong longevity potion keeps him looking barely thirty. He wears his blond hair to the waist and dresses in Parisian noble fashion, short of the absurd; with his firm views on non-interference this has started talk of noble, perhaps Merovingian, blood, which he hears as a charge of bias, one of the few things that angers him. His familiar is a swan and his talisman a sword.

characters.name: Cavillor

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: A younger Transitionalist from the Roman Tribunal who usually defends magi accused before the Tribunal: less practised than Aristarcus, but earnest and dogged for what he thinks right. Some of the pro-Lotharingian magi now retain him as legal adviser, which Proctor is likely to take as a personal betrayal. Clean-shaven, grey-eyed and black-haired, with dark skin he puts down to partly Arab forebears, he dresses plainly in brown. He is married and wears a plain, unenchanted ring. His talisman is a six-ounce iron weight, a Carolingian standard for market weights; he has no familiar.

characters.name: Valerian

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Chief hoplite and enforcer of the Tribunal, the general the Praeco would trust to plan a Wizard's March. A known master of Terram, he is said, like Adanos Lutorum of Exspectatio, to belong to the Guernicus Terrae cult. Slow, methodical and relentless in a hunt, with blunt, physical ideas of justice. Dark-haired and black-eyed, with perfect teeth, he never smiles beyond a quick sideways twitch of the mouth; he wears the covenant's slate-green cloth and, on great occasions, the Tribunal's crimson-and-grey swirled sash of a standing hoplite, edged with leopard fur for his rank. His talisman is a five-foot steel mason's crowbar he walks with. His familiar is an invisible spirit that can move dozens of things at once and seems to fly, and often wears a crow's shape to look less strange. The covenfolk like him, since he leaves their doings alone; he gardens, his tools and methods have eased the gatherers' work, and he mends their homes with rituals.
characters.secrets: No Hermetic magus could bind such a familiar: Valerian is a Mystery Cult initiate, and the crow form hides it.

characters.name: Jerome

params.group: the nobility of France and Flanders

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: The Tribunal's chief go-between with the nobles of France and Flanders, and one of the three who held up Renita's rule, with Proctor and his own former apprentice Eloi of Cunfin. Son of a minor noble, he was left to die by an uncle greedy for his inheritance, found by a Redcap and nursed back by the Jerbiton magus who took him as apprentice. He loves chess, plays it indifferently, keeps many boards in his laboratory and plays by letter with far better players, who like him because he never resigns; they have agreed one day to seek the magic chessboard among the Treasures of Britain. He dresses like a preaching friar rather than a lord, carries a wand, and has a bearded vulture for familiar, its breast turned moss green by what it eats in the swamp.
characters.secrets: Jerome saves 'troublesome heirs', children likely to be killed for their birthright, convinces everyone they are dead with Mentem magic and places them in monasteries or covenants; now and then one is Gifted, as Artorius was. He knows it is very likely a breach of the Code. Proctor does not know. Eloi is his chief partner, and anyone in the network has the Dark Secret Flaw but a strong ally in Jerome. The network may be old: William the Bastard vanished for eight years as a child.

characters.name: Augustina

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: The Traitor of House Tytalus, trained from early apprenticeship for the role by the mater of Buliste, the Prima, and as a hoplite mostly by the previous Traitor. A Traitor volunteers for exile from the House, counts as having lost every contest she was in, and is beneath any Tytalus's notice as a rival; her one duty is to stir the House's contests back to life when they stall, and since Tasgillia's fall she has carried a magical key as her badge of office. The first Traitor, Promethea filia Kalliste, sat out the war on Tasgillia to restore the House if it fell, and became a hoplite and then a Quaesitor; Guernicus sometimes chooses Traitors as Quaesitors, and otherwise accepts them as hoplites. Augustina has spent most of her life in Normandy advising her covenant's leader on Tytalus games; given Proctor's feelings, she gets the riskiest, least trusted assignments. Small and assertive, black-haired and blue-eyed, she often looks tired and happy at once. Her familiar is a small ape; her talisman is a locket on a ribbon or a dagger, nobody knows which, as one is always wound round the other.
characters.secrets: She is a member of the Cabal of Frankish Gold, which works for the Lotharingian Tribunal. She expects it to fail but holds that discontented magi should be able to leave a Tribunal, and wants to see how the Order answers.

characters.summary: Redcap of Dragon's Rest and the Tribunal's Evangelium, the officer, always a Redcap, who travels to every covenant to report the Tourney's results. The book says nothing more of her.

characters.name: Barnabé

description.biography:
A standard grog. His Social Handicap is his arrogance. Athletics is 5, +2 from Puissant Athletics; a fit man runs 10 + (2 x Athletics) miles a day across country, five fewer through wilderness and five more on good roads.
Fist: Init +3, Atk +4, Def +6, Dam 0. Dodge: Init +3, Def +7. Soak +3; Encumbrance 0 (0); Fatigue OK, 0, 0, -2, -4, Unconscious. Wounds: -1 (1-5), -3 (6-10), -5 (11-15), Incapacitated (16-20).

characters.summary: A cursor, the runner a covenant keeps to prove to the Quaesitores that a vis source lies within a day's return march and so is its seisin. Picked as a child for his promise and trained in long-distance running and sprinting, he grew arrogant on the attention, thinks himself indispensable and treats others as his inferiors. His Latin often makes him the magi's interpreter. The book gives him no covenant; place him at yours. An athletic young man with dark hair and a scant beard.

characters.summary: Primus of House Jerbiton, who drew Mathieus back into Hermetic life by asking him to host the Itinerarium, and who trained Constantina. He knows that the last time Paris's ivory dried up the Huns were coming, and would send magi to learn why if it happened again. He does not live in the Tribunal.

characters.summary: Somnifer's filius, found in dreams and trained from the far side of the regio through the enchanted mirror. For the past decade he has represented Lapis Crudus at Tribunal, but he has refused to become a member.

characters.name: Anacrôn, King of the Beggars

description.biography:
Stat block as printed in The Lion and the Lily. Death Prophecy, Personal Vis Source and Painful Magic are his tradition's House Virtues and Flaw. Leadership is 5, +2 from Puissant Leadership. The spell list gives The Irresistible Pressgang as level 40 and The Twisted Spine as MuCo 25, while their own write-ups give CrMe 35 and Mu(Pe)Co 20; the write-ups are used.

Combat: club Init -2, Attack +2, Defence +1, Damage +3; dodge Init -3, Defence 0. Soak +1.

Twilight Scars: his Gift draws vermin instead of repelling them; his breath has the scent of violets; his shadow is the red of blood.

Equipment: a rickety wooden two-wheeled trolley. His talisman is a wand roughly carved from a human leg bone and set with three small bloodstones (+4 destroy human body, +4 blood and wounds), holding two enchantments: Agony of the Uncharitable Stranger (PeCo 30; Voice, Concentration, Individual; Penetration 20, 24 uses a day; racks the target with stabbing pains) and Hobble the Foul-Mouthed Wretch (PeCo 40; Voice, Sun, Individual; Penetration 20, 24 uses a day; lames the target for the duration).

Vis: his Personal Vis Source is the skin he scrapes from his leg stumps, which gives Corpus vis at the price of much pain.

Familiar: Affreux, a brindled mastiff, who can create a ward against people and grow to a bear's size. Magical Animal Companion: Boiteux, Affreux's son. The two pull his trolley.

Each year, vis permitting, he casts The Irresistible Pressgang on at least ten fighting men to make them his cagoux; the five Warping Points it leaves often make them Simple-Minded or similar when it ends.

characters.summary:
An eremite of House Ex Miscellanea who lives on the streets of Paris as King of the Beggars, the Grand Coësre. Bitter, jealous and spiteful, he hates the world and most of humanity. His master took his legs above the knee when he was a boy, in opening him to the Arts, for his tradition's magic rests on pain, hatred and infirmity. He rides a two-wheeled cart drawn by two huge mastiffs: Affreux, his familiar, who can raise a ward that repels people and grow to the size of a bear, and Affreux's son Boiteux, his magical companion. Under the rags and filth he is a handsome, compelling man.

When he grew strong enough to take over the gang that raised him, his pater crowned him king and left Paris, as his own pater had done; where they went, Anacrôn does not know. His family has ruled the beggars for over a century, far longer than Eboris has existed. Through his subjects he can find hands for any job and hears news the Order wants, and sells both for vis and enchantments, mostly to Eboris and Fudarus. He never takes part in the crimes he plans. Twice accused of interfering with mundanes, he was cleared once (no ruin was shown); the second time Harpax of Fudarus declared Wizard's War on the accuser and no charge was ever brought. Many wonder why he has such friends. He and Mathieus are still working out their terms by deed rather than word; both would avoid war, in which Anacrôn has the numbers, the streets and a killer's instinct. Montverte has dealt with him on raids against other covenants' town storehouses.
characters.secrets:
His lineage shares a Death Prophecy: none can die until he is the eldest of the tradition alive. Two of his forebears, his grand-parens's own parens and her mater, survive hidden among his beggars in ruined bodies, riddled with Decrepitude and Warping and longing to die; he will not let them, since each death brings his own nearer. An enemy might strike at him through them.

He knows many dirty secrets of Normandy's magi and has a few genuine allies who value his information. He might draw help from a cabal or Mystery Cult, or be a double agent hunting High Crimes among his apparent friends for the Quaesitores.
