characters.summary: An elderly eremite who spends much of his time at the cathedral school of Laon, respected for his wisdom and the clarity of his writings, and for that long allowed a small vis legacy all to himself. His home is in the city, but his sanctum lies hidden in the mount's rocky cliffs, where the Terram vis is gathered. He wrote of finding a regio, perhaps Divine, at the Templar priory of Nanteuil.

characters.name: Queen Skuld

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely.

characters.summary: Once an unremarkable Tytalus maga of Atramentum, Skuld left her House for Ex Miscellanea in 1178 and vanished a few years later, last seen sailing a small boat through the Channel towards Scandinavia. The Order believes she never came back. She looks about 37. (The book has her living at Atramentum before 1178, though Atramentum was founded only in 1200: a slip it leaves for the storyguide to settle.)
characters.secrets: She returned in 1205 and lives in a regio on the Seine, on a burning longship, as Hierophant of the Children of Odin; she has been Mystagogue at every initiation so far. She claims descent from Rollo and means to be crowned maga-queen of a Normandy taken back from the French king. She may not be the Skuld who left at all, but an impostor: a faerie or magical creature, a powerful hedge wizard (perhaps of the Order of Odin), or a survivor of the Schism War. If the cult's Viking magic is not genuine, she may know it.

characters.name: Porphyrion

description.biography: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal prints no stat block for this magus. These stats are not an official write-up: they are inferred from the book's description by the creation rules. The storyguide may change them freely. The book gives no age: 160 is assumed from the magus's rank.

characters.summary: A powerful Tytalus archmagus who came to Normandy from the Rome Tribunal three years ago and has lived alone since. He may ask to join a young covenant, bringing political and magical weight it could hardly refuse.
characters.secrets: Tytali who have looked into him think he wants the House's leadership, before or more likely after Harpax or Buliste falls, and that joining a weak covenant serves that end. A third contender is the one thing that would make the two Primi work together.

characters.name: Salvirius
characters.summary: Adviser to the Boar King, who looks about fifty and dresses as a hunter or woodsman. He keeps his own road, joins the court only when it is camped, and takes little part in its feasts. A huge scar, like the mark of a spear wound to the heart, crosses his chest, usually hidden. He can grant Virtues by setting a quest that demands a sacrifice: Strong Faerie Blood, Shapeshifter, Animal Ken, Faerie Blood, Second Sight and Wilderness Sense, and the storyguide may add Hermetic ones.
characters.secrets: He may be a faerie, a magus turned faerie, a magus living at the faerie court, or a Diedne refugee from the Schism War. He can teach Diedne Magic, and uses the offer to mark a magus for a watcher who scries the road to the Hill of Martyrs in Paris.

books.name: The library of Fudarus
books.description: The domus magna's library, gathered since 798; the book names none of its books. The magi of Exspectatio, still members of Fudarus, come back regularly to use it and to take books away, and its specialised laboratories draw them too. Exspectatio's oath as vassal gives it access to its liege's books.

books.name: The library of Exspectatio
books.description: The book names no books here. Exspectatio's magi rely on the library of Fudarus, of which they remain members, and fetch books from it on their regular visits. Adanos's own Lab Texts, The Mole's Work, are among the books held for the Tribunal.

books.name: The library of Montverte
books.description: Kept in the central keep under the inner council, and overseen by Runild with the vis stores and the junior magi's donated seasons of labwork. The book does not list its contents; the covenant's great wealth and centuries of raiding suggest a large collection, and its vassals may copy from it under their oath.

books.name: Oleron's library
books.description: The book names no titles. Quintinus inherited the laboratory of a dead member skilled in magical brewing, and the covenant keeps the Queen's designs for the Stone Couches, which he will not discuss.

books.name: Nidi's library
books.description: The book names no titles. Micropedus has written at length on his philosophy of small covenants living in the overlooked spaces of towns, which many of his Bjornaer sodales reject.

books.name: Atsingani's library
books.description: The book names no titles. The covenant has only poor shared tent laboratories; Viviana's laboratory in her faerie wagon is the exception.

books.name: The library of Eboris
books.description: The book names no Hermetic library here, and the covenant does no research. What it has are the few goods Mathieus carried from his fallen covenant in Constantinople and the curiosities he collects for his revels; a storyguide may give it Byzantine letters and art rather than Arts.

books.name: The library of Lapis Crudus
books.description: A large magical library, among the best in the Tribunal before the sealing, with several rare tomes of high quality. During the captivity the magi read it to exhaustion and added many tractatus of their own until their ink and parchment ran out; Somnifer also copied books held up to the mirror, rearranging the mirrored ink by magic. No titles are named. The magi offer seasons of study here to tempt others to take their places.

books.name: Florum's library
books.description: No titles are given. Calvinus spends much of his time in his books, and the covenant's members, drawn from many Houses, follow their own interests: flax and weaving, urban and faerie magic, illusion. Vassals have the right to copy from it under their oath.

books.name: The Spider's Palace's library
books.description: No books are named; the covenant is valued for its laboratories, and its resident magus may copy from Florum's library as a vassal.

books.name: The library of the Donatores
books.description: The tradition's noted collection of Donatores lore on the restless dead and their banishing, its main repository, kept in the catacombs and preserved by Henri. No titles are given; it draws Hermetic interest to an otherwise forgotten covenant.

books.name: The Grail Library
books.description: Celeres's collection on the Grail, Arthur and Merlin, said to hold every book written on the Grail. Few Arthurian works exist in 1220, and the library sorts them into folk tales (mostly Celeres's own transcriptions, in the tale's own tongue with a Latin translation and commentary), Latin British histories, and French romances, his favourites. Magi travel to consult it, and Celeres welcomes the company. His own Grail cycle, unfinished, is kept here too.

books.name: Legends of Brittany
books.author: Celeres of Bonisagus
books.description: A thick book of tales Celeres took down from Breton storytellers, describing many Breton places tied to Arthur and usually to faeries: Arthur's fight with a giant on Mont St. Michel and Merlin's vanishing into Broceliande among them.

books.name: Arthur Among the Britons
books.author: Celeres of Bonisagus
books.description: Welsh tales touching Arthur, among them Culhwch and Olwen, where Arthur's knights win a string of treasures so Culhwch may marry, and the Welsh Triads of things told in threes, with passages from the bard Taliesin.

books.name: The Llancarfan Saints' Lives
books.author: Monks of Llancarfan (twelfth century)
books.description: Lives of Welsh saints that mention Arthur: Cadoc, Padarn, Carannog and, most often, Gildas. They link the folk tales to the histories.

books.name: History of the Britons
books.author: Nennius
books.description: An eighth-century British monk's gathering of whatever he could find on Britain's past, from its founding by Brutus, great-grandson of Aeneas; the oldest account of Arthur's life.

books.name: History of the Kings of Britain
books.author: Geoffrey of Monmouth
books.description: A twelfth-century cleric's great expansion of Nennius, centred on Arthur's deeds and including the Prophecies of Merlin; it ends with Arthur gravely wounded by his nephew Mordred and carried to Avalon to be healed.

books.name: The Lais of Marie de France
books.author: Marie de France
books.description: Songs of love and chivalry by a poet of the court of Marie of Champagne, Eleanor of Aquitaine's daughter. Many began as Breton tales, and their popularity paved the way for the romance.

books.name: Arthurian Romances
books.author: Chretien de Troyes
books.description: Chretien's four great Arthurian poems, Erec and Enide, Cliges, Yvain and Lancelot, on courtly love and the ideals of chivalry.

books.name: Perceval
books.author: Chretien de Troyes
books.description: The unfinished tale of an innocent boy who blunders into knighthood, and the first work to mention the Grail: at a strange castle he sees it but fails to ask about it, leaving the wounded Fisher King unhealed, and sets out to make amends. Chretien died before revealing the Grail's secret, and four later writers have offered endings.

books.name: Joseph d'Arimathie
books.author: Robert de Boron
books.description: Also called the Romance of the Grail: the Grail is the dish of the Last Supper in which Joseph of Arimathea caught Christ's blood, carried after the Resurrection to England and guarded by Joseph's kin down to Perceval. Robert is the first to call it the Holy Grail.

books.name: Parsifal
books.author: Wolfram von Eschenbach
books.description: A German retelling of Perceval that goes its own way: Wolfram's Grail is a stone linked to the heavens, kept in the castle of Munsalvaesche by an order of guardians he calls templeisen (not the Knights Templar), and the poem is rich in alchemy, astrology and Arabic learning.

books.name: Minor works of the Grail Library
books.description: Lesser texts beside the major ones: the Book of Taliesin and the Lives of St. Efflam and St. Illtud among the folk tales; the Annals of Wales, Concerning the Ruin of Britain and the Life of Merlin among the histories; and the Roman de Brut, the continuations of Perceval and Perlesvaus among the romances.

books.name: Library of Atramentum Renatus
books.description: The book names none of the covenant's books. A young, hard-pressed covenant whose resources came from Exspectatio would have a modest collection; Helios's notes on Bibracte and theurgy and Iacula's work on projectiles are its likeliest treasures.

books.name: The library of Confluensis
books.description: The covenant's own library, on the top floor of the Library Tower beside the magical stores; the book calls it beautiful but names none of its books. Under the oath with Dragon's Rest, Redcaps may study here, and Confluensis has let other members of Dragon's Rest study too. Expect strength in the Code of Hermes, Intellego and the Tribunal's records; the covenant makes its own papyrus paper. Its vassals' oath gives them the right to copy from it.

books.name: The Babble Within Thought
books.author: Hicuccus of Criamon
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Worth 23 Build Points.

books.name: The Dismal Itch
books.author: Azenis of Tytalus
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Worth 21 Build Points.

books.name: De Lapii
books.author: Jeremias filius Guernicus
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. A Branch of the Arts (Covenants); worth 31 Build Points.

books.name: Insights from Twilight
books.author: Perpauca of Bonisagus
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. One of the books whose gift began the Library, declared its first tomes in 1081; worth 28 Build Points.

books.name: Mirrors of the Soul
books.author: Perpauca of Bonisagus
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. One of the Library's first tomes; worth 28 Build Points.

books.name: The Mole's Work
books.author: Adanos Lutorum of Tytalus
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Laboratory texts for three spells: Rock of Viscid Clay, Earth That Breaks No More and The Forgiving Earth. Worth 11 Build Points.

books.name: The Peril of Phoebos
books.author: Perpauca of Bonisagus
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. One of the Library's first tomes; worth 11 Build Points.

books.name: The Primal Power
books.author: Peter of Uist
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Worth 26 Build Points.

books.name: Research Notes on Aegis of the Hearth
books.author: Notatus and others
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. A tractatus on Mastery of Aegis of the Hearth, with a laboratory text for a twentieth-level version of the spell bound in. Worth 15 Build Points.

books.name: Subtle Knives
books.author: Jacinda of Flambeau
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Worth 23 Build Points.

books.name: Unveiling the Tempest
books.author: Daniel Tonatris
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Worth 20 Build Points.

books.name: The Library of the Tribunal
books.description: Held for the Tribunal at Confluensis, as a Tourney prize. Begun when Perpauca of Bonisagus, a century and a half ago, tired of her covenant hoarding her books and wrote for the whole Tribunal instead; others followed her. Its list of books and authors is public. Since 1081 its books are Tourney prizes: the winner has sole use of one for seven years under a Cow and Calf Oath (copies belong to the Tribunal) and must return it in good order before the next Tribunal; no one else may read them. A magus who gives the Library an original book may claim, early in the next prize-giving, the lease of one worth as many Build Points, settling rival claims by certamen. A pamphlet on each spine gives readers' comments, enough to judge its Quality and Level. The books recorded here are only a sample of the collection.

creatures.name: Korrigan
creatures.how_many: Bands; they dance in rings at crossroads

powers.name: Human Form
powers.description: Only the stronger korrigan have it. The korred becomes a lovely young woman for an hour, or until it spends the same Might again to change back. In that shape: Int -2, Per +1, Pre +2, Com +1, Str -1, Sta 0, Dex 0, Qik -1, Size 0; Club Init +0, Attack +2, Defense +0, Damage +2; Stone (thrown) Init -1, Attack +3, Defense +1, Damage +1.

creatures.appearance: A stooped little man about three feet high, with a cat's claws for hands and a goat's hooves for feet.
creatures.notes: Might: the book gives typically 5 to 10, rarely 15; 10 is used here. These are the korrigan of Brocéliande, grown dangerous since their queen Viviane lost interest in the forest and them; elsewhere in Brittany (forests, caves, dolmens) they are milder, caring mostly for dancing and hoarded treasure, though still quick to anger. They punish those who vex them, now and then reward someone from their hoard, and invite passers-by into their moonlit dances: those who join may get a gift, those who refuse are punished. Natural weapons: Claws Init -1, Attack +2, Defense +3, Damage +2. Wound penalties: -1 (1-3), -3 (4-6), -5 (7-9), Incapacitated (10-12), Dead (13+). No Virtues or Flaws. The book prints the block under the Rose Coast.
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

creatures.name: The Black Dog

powers.name: Fearsome Bark
powers.description: Animal or Mentem. Works like Panic of the Trembling Heart, but reaches as far as the bark is heard.

powers.name: Dreadful Howl
powers.description: Animal or Mentem. Works like Weight of a Thousand Hells, but lasts until sunrise or sunset and reaches as far as the howl is heard.

creatures.appearance: A black dog, usually a little smaller than a man; rare ones are man-sized (Size 0).
creatures.notes: A Breton folk rite shuts the spirit of a dead relative who will not leave the house into a black dog: the dog is brought indoors, a favourite garment of the dead tied round it, and fed a lump of meat stuffed with plants from the graveyard, then drowned as fast as possible to free the spirit. Until it dies it is the creature here; killed any other way than drowning, it leaves the spirit bound to the spot where it died, and its tongue holds the vis (a drowned dog has none). Its Might is usually 5, up to 10 for a very holy or very wicked dead; a great sinner's spirit gives an Infernal dog, a pagan's (rarely) a Magic one. Natural weapons: Bite Init 0, Attack +3, Defense +1, Damage +1. Wound penalties: -1 (1-4), -3 (5-8), -5 (9-12), Incapacitated (13-16), Dead (17+). The book prints it under the Arrée Mountains, but the rite is used across Brittany.
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

creatures.name: Mogidell, Great Spirit of Ushant

powers.name: Incorporeal
powers.description: Always on. Unseen and untouchable, and beyond the reach of the physical world; a spell can aim at the spirit only if the caster can sense it is there.

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Always on. The spirit knows all that happens on Ushant.

powers.name: Mastery of Mist
powers.description: Costs 1 to 8 points: one per magnitude. Matches any non-Ritual spell of level 40 or less dealing with mist and fog.

creatures.appearance: A vast grey bird filling the sky; when she spreads her wings the sea-fog comes down over Ushant.
creatures.notes: One of the Three Great Spirits of Ushant, a spirit of mist and sea-fog. The book gives the three one shared block (Size, Soak and combat not given; the Virtue is Ways of the Island). Diedne magi summoned them against Fudarus in the Schism War; Primus Klynoites took control of them, and they have been bound into the covenant's walls ever since as genii loci, taking turns to hide Fudarus from chance discovery and opening a way for visitors who give the password. They obey whoever bears the Circlet of the Primus, through the old pact with Fudarus's theurgists rather than the Circlet's own power. Their presence makes 12 pawns of vis appear on Ushant each year, 4 each of Creo, Auram and Imaginem, in a form only Fudarus knows. Mastery powers: the Might cost given here is the least; it rises with the effect's magnitude.
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

powers.name: Incorporeal
powers.description: Always on. Unseen and untouchable, and beyond the reach of the physical world; a spell can aim at the spirit only if the caster can sense it is there.

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Always on. The spirit knows all that happens on Ushant.

powers.name: Mastery of Misdirection
powers.description: Costs 1 to 8 points: one per magnitude. Matches any non-Ritual spell of level 40 or less dealing with misdirection and concealment.

creatures.appearance: A sky-filling shape forever changing between strange blends of man and beast.
creatures.notes: One of the Three Great Spirits of Ushant, a spirit of misdirection. The book gives the three one shared block (Size, Soak and combat not given; the Virtue is Ways of the Island). Diedne magi summoned them against Fudarus in the Schism War; Primus Klynoites took control of them, and they have been bound into the covenant's walls ever since as genii loci, taking turns to hide Fudarus from chance discovery and opening a way for visitors who give the password. They obey whoever bears the Circlet of the Primus, through the old pact with Fudarus's theurgists rather than the Circlet's own power. Their presence makes 12 pawns of vis appear on Ushant each year, 4 each of Creo, Auram and Imaginem, in a form only Fudarus knows. Mastery powers: the Might cost given here is the least; it rises with the effect's magnitude.

powers.name: Incorporeal
powers.description: Always on. Unseen and untouchable, and beyond the reach of the physical world; a spell can aim at the spirit only if the caster can sense it is there.

powers.name: Presence
powers.description: Always on. The spirit knows all that happens on Ushant.

powers.name: Mastery of Storms
powers.description: Costs 1 to 8 points: one per magnitude. Matches any non-Ritual spell of level 40 or less dealing with gales, rain and other foul weather.

creatures.appearance: A vast serpent with a horse's head, filling the sky.
creatures.notes: One of the Three Great Spirits of Ushant, a spirit of stormy weather. The book gives the three one shared block (Size, Soak and combat not given; the Virtue is Ways of the Island). Diedne magi summoned them against Fudarus in the Schism War; Primus Klynoites took control of them, and they have been bound into the covenant's walls ever since as genii loci, taking turns to hide Fudarus from chance discovery and opening a way for visitors who give the password. They obey whoever bears the Circlet of the Primus, through the old pact with Fudarus's theurgists rather than the Circlet's own power. Their presence makes 12 pawns of vis appear on Ushant each year, 4 each of Creo, Auram and Imaginem, in a form only Fudarus knows. Mastery powers: the Might cost given here is the least; it rises with the effect's magnitude.
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

creatures.name: Nain

powers.name: Glittering Treasure
powers.description: Conjures silver coins that gleam in the moonlight among the stones. They vanish at dawn; the Nains use them as bait to draw the greedy into an ambush.

powers.name: Deadly Dance
powers.description: Up to ten victims must dance wildly with the Nains until sunrise. Each hour: Stamina stress roll against 6, or lose a long-term Fatigue level; once unconscious, a Light Wound instead. On a botch, two levels lost per 0 rolled (or the Wound worsens by one level per 0). Many dance to death.

powers.name: Magician's Desire Denied
powers.description: Makes a pebble, leaf or the like seem to hold vis to an Intellego Vim spell. The false vis vanishes at dawn or when Sense the Nature of Vis is cast on it.

creatures.appearance: Imp-like little creatures the size of a child, with long filthy hair, a goat's bowed legs and red eyes that burn like fire.
creatures.notes: The guardians of the stones of Carnac by night, when the Magic aura gives way to an Infernal one. They alone can read the signs traced on the rocks, seen only by starlight on moonless nights, and on their unholy night, the first Wednesday in May, they make blood sacrifices and the Infernal aura rises to 6. They lure the greedy with their false silver and false vis and attack in untrained packs, three to each victim. Natural weapons: Claws Init -1, Attack +2, Defense +3, Damage +2. Wound penalties: -1 (1-3), -3 (4-6), -5 (7-9), Incapacitated (10-12), Dead (13+). No Virtues or Flaws.
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

creatures.name: Lutin
creatures.how_many: Common; one or more to a household

powers.name: The Master's Things
powers.description: Always on, indoors only. The lutin knows everything in the room it is in, how many and where, by look alone, not by use (a wand is just a little stick). It finds things hidden by mundane means or by magic of magnitude 1 or less; to find a person with Magic Resistance it must penetrate.

powers.name: Soap and Suds
powers.description: Indoors only. The floor of the lutin's room turns soapy: anyone moving quickly there, fighting included, rolls Dexterity against 6 each round or slips.

creatures.equipment: Household things: a broom, a shovel or a cloth.
creatures.appearance: A small, servile goblin that looks like a tiny person; it keeps out of sight, even of those who leave it offerings.
creatures.notes: Lutins clean houses in return for offerings of offal or clean water. They are common in Normandy's faerie courts and drawn to villages without a church. All of them dread a 'goblin duke of Normandy', of whom the Order knows nothing. The book gives no Fatigue levels, and Living Language without naming the tongue. Wound penalties: -1 (1-3), -3 (4-6), -5 (7-9), Incapacitated (10-12), Dead (13+). No Virtues or Flaws.
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

creatures.name: The Boar King

powers.name: Voice of the Woods
powers.description: Always on; Animal, Herbam or Mentem. He can speak with any beast or plant of the woods, and they carry out his orders as best they can.

powers.name: Sylvan Sanctity
powers.description: He learns roughly where and how many human intruders are in his forest; too many to follow in full, but he easily spots anyone entering a usually empty part. Must penetrate, though magi's grogs seldom resist. Used daily, and the forest's heart is days deep, so he is ready for visitors.

powers.name: Ancient Rage
powers.description: A frothing fury for a day: +3 to Attack and Soak, -3 to Defense, no Wound Penalties short of Incapacitated. He attacks at the least provocation and may neither retreat nor spare anyone.

powers.name: Impaled by the Thorn
powers.description: Corpus and Mentem. He hurls a boar spear at a human he can see; it hits without a roll, and if it penetrates the victim is frozen, unable to move, sense, think or cast, and does not age. Pulling the spear out ends it but deals a Heavy Wound, unless magic finds a way round that.

powers.name: Call of the Hunter
powers.description: He appears anywhere in his forest.

creatures.equipment: Several boar spears; his court can give him anything else he wants, though some of it may be glamour.
creatures.appearance: A big man with a boar's head, two great tusks thickening his speech, abstract tattoos and bronze rings on his bare arms and chest, hide trousers and a cloak; he rides a wild horse bareback with faerie knights and courtiers about him.
creatures.notes: A faerie the Gauls once worshipped, who claims the Tribunal's forests, hunts boar each autumn and hunts down hunters who take too much. Once allied with House Diedne, he now seeks Merinita or Bjornaer magi to replace them and turn back the clearing of his woods. He has no Virtues or Flaws. The book gives no Fatigue levels. Wound penalties: -1 (1-6), -3 (7-12), -5 (13-18), Incapacitated (19-24), Dead (25+).
creatures.source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal

source: The Lion and the Lily: The Normandy Tribunal, by Atlas Games, open content under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 licence (redcap.org); summarised, not quoted.

buliste.name: Buliste
buliste.summary:
Prima of House Tytalus, Buliste filia Bulcis, who led the House for twenty years before a long Twilight left her seeming dead. She wore the Circlet of the Primus as it began, Harpax could not take it from her, and she wears it still, setting the covenant's invisible spirits to plague her rival: they pull stones from his unfinished tower, put ground glass in his food, sew up his clothes, and play countless other tricks that border on the deadly. More important to the House, she runs Fudarus's vast web of spies and speaks mind to mind with several of its key agents, through her mastery of Mentem and a collection of fixed Arcane Connections; that keeps her respected across the Order, though she has little power in the Normandy Tribunal. Her followers, the Fideli, rally to her purple banner. Her challenges to visitors are philosophical or magical.

She looks a regal woman in her sixties, stout but not fat, in violet satin and white Breton lace, with a very expressive face. Her plainest Twilight scar is that her kindness and her anger can both be felt, the one gently, the other painfully. Older than Harpax, she has the more raw power, but several Twilights have hemmed in her magic.
buliste.secrets: She is steering Harpax toward a Diedne relic so she can frame him with it.

harpax.name: Harpax
harpax.summary:
Primus of House Tytalus, the tenth, Harpax filius Bulcis, who always felt held back by his elder 'sister', fought her hard for the House and lost. When she seemed to die he barely paused before breaking into her sanctum and taking the Rod of the Primus, and took over her role as Lord Heusaff. He torments her with the Rod: one day her sanctum is hot enough to melt her candles, the next she must break ice on her washbasin.

He reads Tribunal politics and his fellow Tytali's plots better than Buliste, governs the covenant's wealth in vis and coin, keeps the oaths of its two vassals, and has bought many magi's loyalty; his Decimi, who wear the tenth Primus's sigil, are the stronger party in Normandy. Without the spies he cannot steer much of the House's business. More careful and more varied than his sister, he has a wider stock of spells and enchantments but less depth in the Arts. His challenges to visitors are physical.

As himself he is a distinguished, stick-thin man who looks about fifty and suffers some arthritis; he keeps other guises too, and may first be met as a butler, a sentry or a tinker. His obsession and sigil is plurality, and his Twilight scar makes the cut of his clothes drift through the day, always in his forest green.
harpax.secrets: As Lord Heusaff he takes the shape of a dashing young nobleman, and has played the part so well that he has had to cultivate unpleasant habits to keep off marriageable women.

adanos_lutorum.name: Adanos Lutorum
adanos_lutorum.summary: Of House Tytalus, the youngest of Exspectatio's founders, with the blood of an earth spirit and a deep affinity for soil, stone and clay: over seven feet tall, entirely hairless, with skin like rock. He has backed Harpax staunchly ever since Buliste refused to take him as her apprentice. In any contest, of blows, words or magic, he lets his opponent wear herself out against his unbreakable defences and then strikes one crushing blow. He is Iasper's master, and wrote The Mole's Work, Terram Lab Texts now held for the Tribunal. Looks about forty.
adanos_lutorum.secrets: Like Valerian of Confluensis, he is reputed to belong to the Guernicus Terrae cult.

kybella.name: Kybella
kybella.summary: Of House Tytalus, a leading member of the Titanoi, the House's cult of theurgists, and a close friend of Prima Buliste. She keeps up the enchantments that hold Fudarus's spirits in check and casts its Aegis of the Hearth each year for both Primi. She specialises in genii loci and searches every place she stays for signs of one. Her filius Helios, of Atramentum Renatus, is a theurgist too. Looks about fifty.
kybella.secrets: Twelve years ago a Twilight showed her Death reaping Europe, kings, bishops, commoners and magi alike, and she founded the Cabal of the Laden Cart to trap Death and hold it to ransom. The other members assume she is one of them but never know which disguise is hers. With another theurgist of her line she is obsessed with the Ankeu, and her agents listen across Brittany for anyone who hears its cart.

geirlaug.name: Geirlaug
geirlaug.summary:
Leader of Montverte for more than half a century, an archmaga of House Flambeau of the founder Harivald's line, plainly a supreme master of Ignem, and the third eldest magus of the Tribunal. Her age is uncertain (perhaps 150, apparently in her mid-sixties). Erratic and marked by long Twilights whose dates no one knows, she hardly ever leaves her tower and is said to have come to depend on fire: great flames are often seen inside it.

She attends council only as an image in a great mirror at the head of the table, an elegant, stern old woman with blazing eyes, the flames behind her moving with her mood: lucid, cryptic, silent or absent. The others privately doubt her sanity, but she tolerates no defiance and the council does her will. She hates Oleron almost beyond reason for an insult from its old leader decades ago, and dislikes the other lieges.

thormod.name: Thormod
thormod.summary: Filius of Geirlaug and her opposite: meticulously neat, his feelings and plans always hidden (he looks 48). Thought to specialise in Perdo, though nothing is really known of his tastes. He never seems to doubt or falter, which makes him secretly the most hated and feared magus of Montverte. He is the covenant's Hermetic ambassador, coldly efficient, and directs its vassals. Alone on the council he seems quite untroubled by Geirlaug and trusts her rule completely; if anyone knows her true state, it is he, and he says nothing.
thormod.secrets: He is a leading member of the Children of Odin, practises Viking magic and bends his influence to the cult's ends; he may be related to its hierophant, Queen Skuld, by blood or by a tryst.

eduardus.name: Eduardus
eduardus.summary:
Steward of the castle, trained in House Jerbiton and a Tytalus for some decades (he looks 43): cultured, artistic and Gently Gifted. As steward he wears the persona of Edward so constantly that no one can tell him from the real Eduardus, of whom little is known. His chief task is to manage the baron, and through him the covenant's dealings with the world; a trusted adviser of the family, he is often at the baron's side. He also keeps the castle running. Edward is sociable, smooth-tongued and a seducer, and the covenfolk women he has charmed bring him the gossip that keeps him informed.

One of the few purple Fideli, who back Buliste as the true Prima of House Tytalus, and a follower of the Hippian school.

runild.name: Runild
runild.summary: The youngest councillor (she looks 43), quiet and unassuming beside the other four. She oversees the covenant's magical resources: its library, its vis stores and the seasons of labwork the junior magi must give. She has just finished training her first apprentice but has no voting sigil of her own yet. Her familiar, a black cat, is descended from Jerbiton's familiar, and she keeps company with all of Montverte's many cats.

caprican_of_merinita.name: Caprican of Merinita
caprican_of_merinita.summary:
Leader and champion of Oleron, apparently about fifty-five, who fought as a mercenary in the wars of the faerie courts in his youth. The last champion, afraid of dying unbeaten (with unknown results), asked him to take the seat. His wife is the faerie queen Lysette and he has an infant daughter, Columbine, whose birth tells him he will likely lose the seat within a few decades.

He follows other magi's careers and gossip closely to guess who his heir will be, and may groom a likely candidate. He dislikes Tytalus magi and would use Wizard's War, even war between covenants, to stop his heir coming from that House, for his daughter must love whoever wins her, and he cannot see how a woman could be happy wed to a creature of strife.

He has Strong Faun Blood, and his magic bends the emotions of people and animals. He belongs to the Keepers of a Thousand Tales.
caprican_of_merinita.secrets: While Fudarus is empty and its leaders feud, he has helped other covenants take its resources and has added and fortified vassals. He expects reprisals if Tytalus finds out, and is untroubled: with Ushant so near, attacks will come anyway.

amelie_of_merinita.name: Amelie of Merinita
amelie_of_merinita.summary:
Oleron's usual spokeswoman and traveller. She is short and slight; river-nymph blood leaves her naturally bald, which she hides with illusory blonde hair, and her fingers and toes are webbed, so she always wears mittens and shoes in public.

She is no great negotiator and knows it, so she lets deals fail or sends partners to Caprican, and uses her office mostly as an excuse to see interesting places and people. Her magic is Aquam, above all the making of unnatural liquids.

quintinus_of_verditius.name: Quintinus of Verditius
quintinus_of_verditius.summary:
An odd Verditius, apparently thirty-five, drawn to Oleron by magical brewing, especially with cider; when a member skilled in such things died he asked to join and take over the dead magus's laboratory. He now builds the new Stone Couches to the Queen's design, finds it far more rewarding than making enchanted items, and may soon ask to change Houses.

He stays out of his House's games of status, which spares him his Housemates' enmity, but his silence about the Couches makes him look idle or incompetent, and his standing in the House is very poor.

regulus_of_merinita.name: Regulus of Merinita
regulus_of_merinita.summary:
The Bee King: blond, amber-eyed and golden-skinned, smelling faintly of candles, and looking no more than twenty-one. His looks come of Strong Faerie Blood: he is a Bee King, a creature so rare that some Merinita think one is made when a young woman swallows a drone from a faerie hive, the steeds of the tiny knights of a sprite queen whose court wanders Mythic Europe.

A Bee King never seems to age but dies of a swift illness a century after birth if nothing kills him first. He can command any bees to do anything they can, even to their deaths, gives long messages through a bee on his tongue, understands hives and reads the bees he touches, and is never stung. He turns the grove's Herbam vis into honey holding Animal vis, and his bees build the wax statues in the chase.
regulus_of_merinita.secrets: Two Bee Kings can never meet: if Regulus comes within scent of the hive-girl he will fall into a murderous rage and have to kill her. She is the child of faeries like him, or his own by some forgotten affair; he wants her raised happily far away, and watched, for he has never heard of a human Bee Queen.

luna_of_bjornaer.name: Luna of Bjornaer
luna_of_bjornaer.summary:
A noble rat. Born in Sicily of mixed Italian and Arab stock, dark-haired and dark-eyed and just under five feet tall, she dresses in few layers so as to slip in and out of her heartbeast. She has no talisman yet and is looking for something to enchant.

She trained first in the Beast Master tradition of House Ex Miscellanea; Micropedus drew out her heartbeast and got her accepted, if not respected, in his House, whose members think a rat heartbeast freakish. She thinks rats noble: sneaky, tenacious, hardy and made for living beside wasteful humans. Micropedus grooms her as his heir. At least an hour a week, and whenever she is stressed, she sits as a rat on a rafter of the covenant's granary gazing at more food than a rat could eat in a century.

Animal is her best Art, the rest learned piecemeal for useful tricks. She has mastered a spell to tunnel through stone or wood in rat form. Her combat spells are weak, but she can still call and command animals and defends herself with hordes of rats.

micropedus_of_bjornaer.name: Micropedus of Bjornaer
micropedus_of_bjornaer.summary:
The Starling, Nidi's leader, apparently sixty. He spends much of his time as a bird and finds it ever harder, slower and more painful to change back as his Warping grows; a Twilight Scar leaves patches of feathers on his scalp in human form. His name, small feet, comes from another scar: his heartbeast looks like the footless starling of folklore, and his feet have shrunk with age to a child's; he suspects they will drop off when he enters Final Twilight.

The idea that small covenants can live in the uncharted spaces of towns is his. He has written on it at length and trained a few apprentices, though many Bjornaer reject it. An Auram magus skilled at weather, he breaks droughts with rain and kills grain blight with frost; the prosperity this brought is arguably why a town grew so close to the covenant.

viviana_of_ex_miscellanea.name: Viviana of Ex Miscellanea
viviana_of_ex_miscellanea.summary: Spiritual leader and guide of Atsingani, a fading beauty of Mediterranean blood who looks about forty-one: filia of Aureliana, the eldest of the founders, and a soothsayer and healer of the same Byzantine tradition. She owns the covenant's most prized possession, a grand wagon of faerie make, far larger inside than out and richly fitted, with room for a laboratory and a bedchamber; it never runs out of fresh clothes and linen for her, and rides so smoothly over rough roads that nothing inside is jolted.

jacques_of_flambeau.name: Jacques of Flambeau
jacques_of_flambeau.summary: Captain of the covenant's mercenaries, apparently thirty-nine. Already a seasoned Brabançon warrior, he was apprenticed at eighteen to an Ex Miscellanea eremite, so he is only some ten years past his Gauntlet. As soon as he became a magus he left his pater's covenant to rejoin his own people, and soon after joined House Flambeau. He burns to avenge his father on the Capuchonnes who killed him in 1183.

mathieus_of_constantinople.name: Mathieus of Constantinople
mathieus_of_constantinople.summary:
Leader of Eboris and Warden of Paris, an archmagus, filius of Maria of Constantinople; apparent age 65. A scion of a Constantinopolitan noble house who plays the exiled lord, he follows the Jerbiton idea of sufficiency: he knows enough magic to live as he likes, and more study would only fool bigger crowds or win more certamen. Long bored by magic, he spent years in the vices of the rich; now he has goals he doubts he will reach.

He backs the French crown, whose strength is remaking Paris into a city that could foster great beauty, which sets him against agents of the great dukes, of England and of Italian princes. He backs the Antigones, the rising Jerbiton generation, hoping they will mend an Order he thinks the best but a weak tool for peace. And he loathes Venice and the covenants he blames for the Fourth Crusade, supporting the French Church as a weight against Venice's hold on the pope and distrusting the Roman covenants with chapter houses in Venice. He is a master of illusion and of casting in a city.
mathieus_of_constantinople.secrets: He named Constantina his heir mostly to stop people pestering him, and could be talked into naming someone who offers him a genuinely new experience.

marcus_of_paris.name: Marcus of Paris
marcus_of_paris.summary:
Redcap and Mathieus's chief servant, the majordomo of Eboris (the book does not say whether he has the Gift). He sells news of Paris to other covenants, haggling every contract, from a weekly letter to the recovery of private papers, and sometimes passes the work to the young magi. When the nobles go home to their own lands he hires local magi's servants to keep watch on them for his clients.

He also recruits: of the many odd characters who drift to Paris he picks the best, teaches some a little Latin and places them with covenants across the Tribunal for a fee from either side. A young covenant can get a full household from him, of very colourful pasts.

constantina_filia_andru.name: Constantina filia Andru
constantina_filia_andru.summary: A young firebrand of House Jerbiton, trained by the Primus Andru himself, and Mathieus's designated heir to Eboris, a choice he made largely to annoy the magi badgering him to pick one. The book does not say where she lives.

andru.name: Andru
andru.summary: Primus of House Jerbiton, who drew Mathieus back into Hermetic life by asking him to host the Itinerarium, and who trained Constantina. He knows that the last time Paris's ivory dried up the Huns were coming, and would send magi to learn why if it happened again. He does not live in the Tribunal.

somnifer_of_merinita.name: Somnifer of Merinita
somnifer_of_merinita.summary:
A master of dream magic, apparent age 30. During the captivity he sent his mind out in spirit form into the dreams of those he met and so kept the covenant informed of the world. He found his apprentice Languidus through dreams, lured him to the regio and trained him through the mirror in the hut that was his schoolroom and scriptorium. Warping blurs dream and waking for him, and it is hard to tell whether he is awake or sleepwalking.

With Renita dead and Stellatus gone to Iberia, he is next after Celeres of Cunfin in the line of eldest magi from which the Praeco is named.
somnifer_of_merinita.secrets: Proctor, who wants a Praeco he can trust or control, finds Somnifer as awkward a choice as Celeres.

mnemon_of_tytalus.name: Mnemon of Tytalus
mnemon_of_tytalus.summary: A master of Rego, apparent age 60. He was a year short of his Gauntlet when the regio closed (the book's age for him fits that badly), and has never really lived his House's culture of conflict. Searching for a way out, he grew expert in spells of transport; he made the mirror that is now the covenant's gate and negotiated the new terms with Candidus. Walking and running exasperate him, and he has an unsettling habit of popping across a room or snapping objects into his hand.
mnemon_of_tytalus.secrets: Nobody knows what he promised Candidus. Once someone takes his place he must carry out a fearsome task the faerie bound him to, which could fall on a player covenant.

languidus_of_merinita.name: Languidus of Merinita
languidus_of_merinita.summary: Somnifer's filius, found in dreams and trained from the far side of the regio through the enchanted mirror. For the past decade he has represented Lapis Crudus at Tribunal, but he has refused to become a member.

rhesus.name: Rhesus
rhesus.summary: Leader of Florum's magi: clean-shaven and muscular, looking about fifty-four. He came from the Roman Tribunal, partly to escape the professional jealousies of his House and partly because he is a weaver himself and wanted to study the spider-kin; the magical uses of flax are his chief interest. He backs the Lotharingian cause because he is weary of Normandy's ways, which make him defend resources that any other Tribunal would simply grant him.

calvinus.name: Calvinus
calvinus.summary: A middle-aged magus with the Gentle Gift, looking about forty-five. Ghent knows him as 'Uncle Calvin', younger brother of Piet de Spinnen's late father, back from decades of trade in Italy, whose money is said to have paid for the Farm's last building; Piet plainly heeds his advice. A private man who reads a great deal and is said to speak five languages, he often negotiates or interprets for his nephew. Trained in urban magic like many Jerbiton, he is skilled at illusion, at spying on the covenant's mundane rivals, and at arranging crimes. His apprentice Sophia is charming and as bookish as he is, so that her cousins fear she will never marry.
calvinus.secrets: Piet is really his son Petrus. His Italian wife was invented, and the 'daughter' who has just arrived in Ghent, supposedly raised by equally invented grandparents, is Sophia.

alroy.name: Alroy
alroy.summary: Florum's champion, for Normandy's habit of fighting over resources means most covenants need one: an older Flambeau, looking about sixty, with a distinguished war record in the Levant. Five years ago he decided to take an apprentice and chose Florum because it was rich, comfortable, far from the Saracens, and offered the odd Tourney. He has outlived his own expectations and killed most of what once frightened him; he hopes raising an apprentice and fighting Tytalus magi will rekindle him, a man of eager passions trying to shake off a veteran's boredom.

prunellie.name: Prunellie
prunellie.summary:
An elderly maga, looking about sixty-one, who travels the Low Countries studying their peculiar faerie realm. Here, she teaches, the old gods and ancestral trees made a pact with the coming Church: faeries helped spread the Dominion and tame the forests, teaching men to clear woods, plough, sow wheat and flax and drive piles for dikes; one brought flax, a gnome invented starch, and the kabouters, a dwarfish folk, gave a hundred bells to the missionaries they favoured, and sang the first carillon of the Low Countries under a gnome's baton. Faeries who refused were hunted down by saints whom the friendly ones guided, and lie now as lone stones in the fields.

Her House thinks her interest in urban faeries a little odd, but she is firmly allied with a tribe of kabouters and has taught others her urban faerie magic. She picked the Farm's site over an old kabouter workshop. She backs the Lotharingian Tribunal because she believes the faeries' strange surrender to the Divine belongs to Flanders, Brabant and perhaps Frisia alone.
prunellie.secrets: She could restore the stone faeries but usually harvests them for vis instead.

eulogius.name: Eulogius
eulogius.summary: Leader of Requies Aeterna and perhaps the last founder of the Donatores living; his age is uncertain, and he looks a hundred and four. His great days of hunting the restless dead are long past, and Final Twilight is probably near. His worst Twilight scars are a body slowly turning to a corpse, impossibly gaunt with dead, withered skin, and a pain in sunlight that keeps him in his underground sanctum. He remains an unequalled banisher, a master of Perdo, Corpus and Mentem.

henri.name: Henri
henri.summary: Eulogius's youngest filius and his helper, a Donator who stays mostly from duty to his tradition, and has made himself keeper of the covenant's library and lore for the generations to come.

norlanus.name: Norlanus
norlanus.summary: An elderly eremite who spends much of his time at the cathedral school of Laon, respected for his wisdom and the clarity of his writings, and for that long allowed a small vis legacy all to himself. His home is in the city, but his sanctum lies hidden in the mount's rocky cliffs, where the Terram vis is gathered. He wrote of finding a regio, perhaps Divine, at the Templar priory of Nanteuil.

eloi.name: Eloi
eloi.summary:
Founder of Cunfin and the man who holds it together, looking about fifty-two. To the monks he is Brother Eligius, their prior, loved for his devotion and sought for his wise counsel; to the magi he is a magus deeply anxious about the Order's standing with the Church. He sees himself as a follower of St. Nerius, bridging the Magic and the Divine, and his charm and faith bind the covenant's quarrelsome members together.

A younger son of minor nobles meant for the priesthood, he was found by Jerome of Jerbiton and trained as a magus instead, serving Jerome usefully at Confluensis but never reconciling his Gift with his wish to serve God. Meeting Angelus in 1191 showed him a way: he joined the abbey, founded the covenant with Jerome's blessing, and was soon elected prior. He uses Holy Influence to calm the Dominion about the abbey.

Close to the Priory of St. Nerius without belonging to it, he wants Nerius recognised by the Latin Church, but above all wants peace between Order and Church, and uses his weight in the Cistercian Order to head off quarrels between magi and clergy. With Jerome and Proctor he was one of the three pillars of the late Praeco's Tribunal, its link to the Church. His present worry is the new Dominicans and their zeal against heresy.
eloi.secrets: He is Jerome's chief partner in hiding rescued heirs, which is very likely a breach of the Code; it brought Artorius to Cunfin.

angelus.name: Angelus
angelus.summary:
A holy hermit of House Ex Miscellanea who looks about seventy-five and lives alone in a cave above the abbey, contemplating God. The Order's only record of him is from the Tribunal of 1144, where he appeared once and then dropped out of sight; he had not left his cave for decades when Eloi found him in 1191, told him of St. Nerius and showed him the abbey and its regio. At the next Tribunal Cunfin was recognised with the two of them as founders.

He holds that Magic flows from the Divine and that Twilight is a glimpse of the face of God: a blessing God gives, but one it is sinful to seek, since only God judges who is worthy. He takes little part in the covenant's affairs, though Eloi and even Celeres come to him for counsel. He alone of Cunfin's magi lacks the Gentle Gift.
angelus.secrets: He will not speak of his lineage; Eloi believes his parens was Valoran, filius of St. Nerius himself.

celeres.name: Celeres
celeres.summary:
A magus of House Bonisagus perhaps a hundred and fifty years old (the book is not sure) and looking a hundred: since Renita's death and Stellatus's departure for Iberia, the eldest magus of the Tribunal and so first in line to be Praeco, to the dismay of Confluensis, whose magi fear his eccentricity and his hold over Cunfin's Redcaps.

Late in the twelfth century he found a copy of Chretien's Perceval and was seized by the riddle of the Grail. He gathered every book on Arthur, the Round Table and the Grail he could, and when he heard of Cunfin, with its monks and holy hermit, it seemed a page from the romances: he came at once in 1199 and talked Eloi into admitting him. He rebuilt the regio as a castle and calls the Redcaps his knights, who bring him every rumour of the Grail.

No longer hoping to find it, he now thinks the Grail may be beyond finding, and wants instead to understand it and share what he learns. He is writing a great Grail cycle on its spiritual meaning, coloured by Cistercian thought, and hopes his last apprentice Artorius will finish it if he cannot. Many doubt his wits; no one doubts his scholarship. He has the Gentle Gift, a playful humour, and is one of the covenant's champion hastiludium team.

artorius_filius_celeres.name: Artorius filius Celeres
artorius_filius_celeres.summary: A magus of House Bonisagus newly through his Gauntlet. Eloi brought him to Cunfin as an orphan of sixteen, meaning to train him as his own successor, but Celeres announced he needed a squire and claimed the boy as his own apprentice. At his Gauntlet, his knighting as Celeres puts it, his parens named him after the legendary king of Britain. He has the Gentle Gift; his plans are his own.
artorius_filius_celeres.secrets: He is one of the heirs Jerome saved from death for their birthright and hid with Eloi's help; whose heir he is, the book does not say.

vrard_de_tours.name: Évrard de Tours
vrard_de_tours.summary:
Redcap of House Mercere and the Tribunal's senior Redcap, the only one at Cunfin who served at the old Mercer House in Tours. He moved the House to Cunfin, rebuilt its network and trained its Redcaps, and now wants to retire: his only duty is to watch over the Mercere Portal to Dragon's Rest. He looks under fifty, having begun a longevity ritual late in life.

He trained both Cunfin's other Redcaps, his son Hervé and the foundling Renaud, and passed his post at the fairs to Hervé. After so long in a monastery he finds Celeres's playful humour a relief and spends much time with him.

renaud_fouinon.name: Renaud Fouinon
renaud_fouinon.summary: Redcap of House Mercere, a foundling Eloi brought to the covenant, trained by Évrard and raised as Hervé's foster brother. Naturally clever, he drank and slept his way through the University of Paris and joined the Goliards, which most likely cost him the post at the Champagne fairs that went to Hervé. He now roams France enjoying himself, and is proud to be one of Cunfin's hastiludium team with Celeres and Eloi, which has won three times running.

helios_filius_kybella.name: Helios filius Kybella
helios_filius_kybella.summary: A theurgist of House Tytalus and co-founder of both Atramentum and Atramentum Renatus. He is fascinated by the schemes of the fallen Diedne covenant of Bibracte and its cult of Vercingetorix, and is trying to learn whether its magi succeeded in raising the hero's spirit.

gulo_midusulfis.name: Gulo Midusulfis
gulo_midusulfis.summary: A magus of House Bjornaer and co-founder of Atramentum and Atramentum Renatus. A Quaesitor wants to know whether the reports of a wild beast ravaging the country round the covenant mean that Gulo has broken the Code.

iacula.name: Iacula
iacula.summary: A maga of House Bonisagus who joined Atramentum Renatus after its founding. She is absorbed in the study of how thrown and shot things fly, and her research has produced several spells with great martial potential.

philip.name: Philip
philip.summary: A magus of House Ex Miscellanea and one of the Donatores, a tradition that seeks to lay the restless dead to rest. Lately of Requies Aeterna, he has only just joined Atramentum Renatus. He shares Helios's interest in Bibracte but fears his colleague's work is stirring its ghosts to anger.

proctor.name: Proctor
proctor.summary: Presiding Quaesitor of the Normandy Tribunal for its last two meetings and, since Renita's death, acting leader of Confluensis. Against his House's custom of rotating the post, he seems unlikely to let anyone else be chosen next time; his filius Aristarcus would follow him. Tytalus diabolists killed his grandparens, and his parens passed on a hatred of that House, so he deeply mistrusts the Tribunal's Tytalus magi. A strict upholder of the Code and a firm Transitionalist, he may yet be driven to extreme measures by his suspicion. He looks about sixty: weathered face, leathery hands, pale skin, a white beard and no moustache, and a favourite slate-green robe fastened with two crossed pins shaped as swan feathers, one lead and one ivory. His familiar is a sacred ibis from his wandering youth. His talisman is a brass fool's bell that jingles in his pocket; he believes it one of the bells Richard the Devil wore doing penance in Rome, and it is enchanted against the Infernal. Those he distrusts are not told, and many think he carries it as a reminder not to act the fool.

aristarcus.name: Aristarcus
aristarcus.summary: Filius of Proctor and the Tribunal's usual prosecutor, with unrivalled rhetoric. He does not share his parens's distrust of House Tytalus and leans Traditionalist, but the two are frequent allies in their faith in the law. A strong longevity potion keeps him looking barely thirty. He wears his blond hair to the waist and dresses in Parisian noble fashion, short of the absurd; with his firm views on non-interference this has started talk of noble, perhaps Merovingian, blood, which he hears as a charge of bias, one of the few things that angers him. His familiar is a swan and his talisman a sword.

cavillor.name: Cavillor
cavillor.summary: A younger Transitionalist from the Roman Tribunal who usually defends magi accused before the Tribunal: less practised than Aristarcus, but earnest and dogged for what he thinks right. Some of the pro-Lotharingian magi now retain him as legal adviser, which Proctor is likely to take as a personal betrayal. Clean-shaven, grey-eyed and black-haired, with dark skin he puts down to partly Arab forebears, he dresses plainly in brown. He is married and wears a plain, unenchanted ring. His talisman is a six-ounce iron weight, a Carolingian standard for market weights; he has no familiar.

valerian.name: Valerian
valerian.summary: Chief hoplite and enforcer of the Tribunal, the general the Praeco would trust to plan a Wizard's March. A known master of Terram, he is said, like Adanos Lutorum of Exspectatio, to belong to the Guernicus Terrae cult. Slow, methodical and relentless in a hunt, with blunt, physical ideas of justice. Dark-haired and black-eyed, with perfect teeth, he never smiles beyond a quick sideways twitch of the mouth; he wears the covenant's slate-green cloth and, on great occasions, the Tribunal's crimson-and-grey swirled sash of a standing hoplite, edged with leopard fur for his rank. His talisman is a five-foot steel mason's crowbar he walks with. His familiar is an invisible spirit that can move dozens of things at once and seems to fly, and often wears a crow's shape to look less strange. The covenfolk like him, since he leaves their doings alone; he gardens, his tools and methods have eased the gatherers' work, and he mends their homes with rituals.
valerian.secrets: No Hermetic magus could bind such a familiar: Valerian is a Mystery Cult initiate, and the crow form hides it.

jerome.name: Jerome
jerome.summary: The Tribunal's chief go-between with the nobles of France and Flanders, and one of the three who held up Renita's rule, with Proctor and his own former apprentice Eloi of Cunfin. Son of a minor noble, he was left to die by an uncle greedy for his inheritance, found by a Redcap and nursed back by the Jerbiton magus who took him as apprentice. He loves chess, plays it indifferently, keeps many boards in his laboratory and plays by letter with far better players, who like him because he never resigns; they have agreed one day to seek the magic chessboard among the Treasures of Britain. He dresses like a preaching friar rather than a lord, carries a wand, and has a bearded vulture for familiar, its breast turned moss green by what it eats in the swamp.
jerome.secrets: Jerome saves 'troublesome heirs', children likely to be killed for their birthright, convinces everyone they are dead with Mentem magic and places them in monasteries or covenants; now and then one is Gifted, as Artorius was. He knows it is very likely a breach of the Code. Proctor does not know. Eloi is his chief partner, and anyone in the network has the Dark Secret Flaw but a strong ally in Jerome. The network may be old: William the Bastard vanished for eight years as a child.

augustina.name: Augustina
augustina.summary: The Traitor of House Tytalus, trained from early apprenticeship for the role by the mater of Buliste, the Prima, and as a hoplite mostly by the previous Traitor. A Traitor volunteers for exile from the House, counts as having lost every contest she was in, and is beneath any Tytalus's notice as a rival; her one duty is to stir the House's contests back to life when they stall, and since Tasgillia's fall she has carried a magical key as her badge of office. The first Traitor, Promethea filia Kalliste, sat out the war on Tasgillia to restore the House if it fell, and became a hoplite and then a Quaesitor; Guernicus sometimes chooses Traitors as Quaesitors, and otherwise accepts them as hoplites. Augustina has spent most of her life in Normandy advising her covenant's leader on Tytalus games; given Proctor's feelings, she gets the riskiest, least trusted assignments. Small and assertive, black-haired and blue-eyed, she often looks tired and happy at once. Her familiar is a small ape; her talisman is a locket on a ribbon or a dagger, nobody knows which, as one is always wound round the other.
augustina.secrets: She is a member of the Cabal of Frankish Gold, which works for the Lotharingian Tribunal. She expects it to fail but holds that discontented magi should be able to leave a Tribunal, and wants to see how the Order answers.

myrina.name: Myrina
myrina.summary: Redcap of Dragon's Rest and the Tribunal's Evangelium, the officer, always a Redcap, who travels to every covenant to report the Tourney's results. The book says nothing more of her.

queen_skuld.name: Queen Skuld
queen_skuld.summary: Once an unremarkable Tytalus maga of Atramentum, Skuld left her House for Ex Miscellanea in 1178 and vanished a few years later, last seen sailing a small boat through the Channel towards Scandinavia. The Order believes she never came back. She looks about 37. (The book has her living at Atramentum before 1178, though Atramentum was founded only in 1200: a slip it leaves for the storyguide to settle.)
queen_skuld.secrets: She returned in 1205 and lives in a regio on the Seine, on a burning longship, as Hierophant of the Children of Odin; she has been Mystagogue at every initiation so far. She claims descent from Rollo and means to be crowned maga-queen of a Normandy taken back from the French king. She may not be the Skuld who left at all, but an impostor: a faerie or magical creature, a powerful hedge wizard (perhaps of the Order of Odin), or a survivor of the Schism War. If the cult's Viking magic is not genuine, she may know it.

porphyrion.name: Porphyrion
porphyrion.summary: A powerful Tytalus archmagus who came to Normandy from the Rome Tribunal three years ago and has lived alone since. He may ask to join a young covenant, bringing political and magical weight it could hardly refuse.
porphyrion.secrets: Tytali who have looked into him think he wants the House's leadership, before or more likely after Harpax or Buliste falls, and that joining a weak covenant serves that end. A third contender is the one thing that would make the two Primi work together.
